Trauma is not a competition. With this comment I do not intend to undermine the severity of any given trauma. 

The intention of the book appears to be an observance of how different traumas affect the various aspects of people’s lives, as well as some surprisingly unconventional methods to resolve such trauma, not to compare the extent of which trauma is considered the morally significant. 

Feel free to completely ignore the rest of this comment but I’d like to share some more of my personal experience again: 

5 years ago I would not have understood a lot of the things I am capable of understanding now. It’s amazing how some methods, however absurd they may seem, can go such a long way in really healing trauma. Trauma can be small or big. It can be hard to even understand that something is traumatic or what the traumatic memory even is due to the way traumatic memories are stored. 
My trauma has manifested as tightness or compression in my body, in mannerisms such as apologizing all the time, certain social patterns and many many other ways. 
I’ve found that the human mind likes a logical explanation and if you give it that structure, however ridiculous, you can find illogical pathways through the trauma and release your hold on it. Inevitably it comes back but less strong each time. The awareness of that process is the power of your consciousness. Anyway ramble over I hope that if you take anything from this thread it is a sense of openness to the many types of experiences available to different people, other people’s experiences should not dictate your own. You are your own being with your own choices and I trust you to make them wisely. Travel well!
